review_notes:
I read the whole target file and the imported StrongOperatorLimit.lean. I also checked how PositiveShift is defined (it is an abbrev for Set.Ioi (0:ℝ)) and where naturalShift is used. The new definitions are naturalShift, yosidaOperatorSequence and yosidaStrongLimit.

- naturalShift is the sequence n+1 as an element of PositiveShift. I found no Mathlib equivalent and no competing copy elsewhere in the repo. Other files only use it.
- yosidaOperatorSequence is a thin named wrapper that fixes the time t. It is used as the argument of strongOperatorLimit.
- yosidaStrongLimit is built from the existing strongOperatorLimit, which itself uses Mathlib's ContinuousLinearMap.ofTendstoOfBoundedRange. It is a specialisation, not an independent version of an existing concept.

I did not search all of Mathlib for a ready-made strong-limit construction for contraction sequences. Mathlib does not seem to have one with this Cauchy and contraction packaging, so I report nothing.
